title: Aftershock capacity recovery and tenant fairness plan
creator: Marco Ruiz
description:
Summary:
During the hosted API capacity incident on 2026-03-07 we observed a multi-stage GPU exhaustion sequence: an initial tenant burst saturated a subset of pools, autoscaler hysteresis delayed priming of spare capacity, and a cache-invalidation regression caused disproportionate KV cache churn which amplified per-request GPU time. The result was sustained queue buildup, aggressive per-tenant throttling, and increased 500/429 rates for latency-sensitive customers.

Root causes and contributing factors: 
- Tenant burst pattern: a small number of tenants executed simultaneous large-context generations (image+text) which multiplied token compute. Tenancy signals did not capture sudden sequence-length correlated spikes.
- Autoscaler hysteresis: conservative downscale/upscale thresholds plus long cool-down windows prevented rapid slot priming when utilization rose.
- KV cache regression: a prior change (runtime-1.22) introduced a policy that evicted cache entries on certain error paths, causing high cache-miss rates and longer decode loops.
- Admission control gap: global admission logic prioritized throughput over fairness; no short-term per-tenant soft-caps existed to dampen localized storms.

Goal: implement a targeted, low-risk remediation bundle that reduces tail GPU exhaustion risk and restores predictable latency for SLO-bound customers while we design longer-term scheduling changes. Remediations should be reversible and have clear telemetry.

Planned action items (short horizon):
1) Adaptive headroom: tune autoscaler to maintain a transient spare slot buffer (slot-headroom) that is proportional to recent spike variance for each region. Conservative rollout to 10% capacity in host pools.
2) Tenant soft-band throttles: add a fast-path that applies a short-lived soft token budget per-tenant when sequence-length-weighted QPS exceeds a threshold. This is a black-box admission policy implemented in the gateway layer (does not change GPU runtime).
3) KV cache rollback + targeted fix: revert the eviction-on-error policy to prior stable behavior, and add an automated canary that detects sudden cache miss-rate increases.
4) Rapid scale bypass: a one-off operator API to temporarily allow immediate scale-to request when latency SLOs breach a critical threshold (requires guardrails, RBAC, and an audit log).
5) Post-deploy chaos test and replay: run a deterministic tenant-burst replay in staging with increased sequence-length variance and measure queue growth.

Acceptance criteria are below. Implementation notes: items (1) and (2) must include a feature-flagged rollout. Item (3) will be first to deploy because it reduces per-token cost and is reversible with minimal risk. Item (4) requires runbook updates and a short security review.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Increasing headroom raises short-term unit costs; we will monitor cost and limit to 10% cap for the pilot.
- Tenant soft-band throttles may increase 429s for heavy tenants; we will provide informative error payloads and customer notifications for high-impact accounts.
- Rapid scale bypass must be guarded to prevent runaway provisioning and billing surprises.

Deliverables: compact runbook updates, telemetry dashboards for the new headroom metric, an admission-service feature flag, a KV-cache revert PR, and an incident playbook addendum.
acceptance_criteria: KV cache revert deployed to prod behind feature flag and observed cache-miss rate returns to baseline (< baseline*1.1) within 1 hour of deploy
Autoscaler headroom feature toggled in two regions with headroom <= 10% and no instability during 72h observation
Tenant soft-band throttles active behind flag; automated canary demonstrates 30% reduction in tail queue length under synthetic burst without increasing global 95th latency > 10%
Operator rapid-scale bypass API implemented with RBAC and audit logging; tested in staging and exercise runbook documented
Post-deploy staging replay shows queue growth curve reduced vs pre-fix and runbook updated with precise SLIs/SLOs and rollback steps
